title: Expand a compressed banner
prompt:
Expand a compressed banner in which k[text] means text repeated k times and groups can nest, so 2[a3[b]] becomes abbbabbb.

- s has 0 to 2,000 characters: lowercase letters, digits, [ and ]. It is always well-formed.
- Every [ is preceded by a repeat count k between 1 and 99 (one or two digits); digits appear nowhere else.
- The expanded result has at most 100,000 characters. Return it as a string.
hints: When you hit ], which group is ending? The innermost one, the one opened most recently.
Keep a stack of (text built so far, repeat count) for each open group, and build the current group's text separately.
On [, push the current text and count and start fresh. On ], pop (prev, k) and set current = prev + current repeated k times. Remember counts can have two digits.

solution.explanation: A stack holds the partially built text and repeat count of every enclosing group. Opening a group saves the current state and starts empty; closing one repeats the inner text and appends it to the saved outer text. Digits are accumulated so multi-digit counts work.

complexity.notes: L is the output length and d the nesting depth: each closing bracket copies at most the text of its own level, so no level copies more than L characters.

followUps: Write the recursive-descent version. What does the call stack replace?
Return only the character at position p without building the whole string.
